questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- If the file is outside the working directory, you must Read it in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: ListAgents

Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 15 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

eaaf6202 2026-09-16
Use one schema fallback on both canvas load paths

readDocumentRecords, the path that runs when the backing markdown changes
on disk, had its own copy of the fallback and still substituted the full
current schema. Both call sites now share schemaBeforeAppMigrations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

f45e008a 2026-09-16
Hoist link icon to icons.ts, and replay app migrations for schema-less files

The icon SVG now follows the TOOL_ARROW_ICON_SVG pattern and is applied
inline the way tldraw's own HyperlinkButton does, so the vendored
tl-hyperlink__icon class supplies size and color and the data URI is no
longer duplicated in styles.css.

processInitialData's schema fallback now drops only this plugin's own
sequence ids. Substituting the full current schema told loadSnapshot the
records were already migrated, so the url backfill was skipped and
store.put threw.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.text:
I have the picture. No changes made — here's the state and the plan.

## Where PR [#1442](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1442) stands

CI is **fully green**. It's blocked purely on `CHANGES_REQUESTED` from mdroidian — 3 unresolved comments, all landed 2026-09-22. Branch is **52 commits behind main**; only `styles.css` is touched on both sides and it looks auto-mergeable.

Head is now `eaaf6202`, two commits beyond what I pushed. A later session added `f45e008a` and `eaaf6202`, which fixed review finding #9 (the schema fallback). **All three of Michael's comments are on that work**, not on the link feature.

## The three comments, assessed honestly

**1. `canvasFileSync.ts:70` — "How is this related to adding link support on text shapes?"**

Fair, and I'd concede the framing. It isn't directly related; it's fallout. Making `url` *required* turned a previously-harmless missing-schema case into "canvas won't open". But here's the fact that matters: `createRawTldrawFile` (`tldraw.ts:112`) **always** writes `schema`. This plugin never produces a schema-less file. That path is reachable only via hand-editing, corruption, or a file written by the *other* tldraw-in-obsidian plugin — which `TldrawRawData`'s own comment says we deliberately follow.

**2. `tldraw.ts:57` — "Is this from tldraw docs or something Claude cooked up?"**

Cooked up. There's no tldraw doc for `schemaBeforeAppMigrations`. The *mechanism* is real and I verified it in-app earlier in this PR — retroactive sequences replay only when absent from the loaded schema, so listing them at current version makes `loadSnapshot` skip the backfill and the next `store.put` throws. But right now nothing pins that, which is exactly why the question is reasonable.

**3. `tldraw.ts:90` — "legacy?"**

He's right. The comment calls the stored schema "the legacy on-disk format"; it isn't legacy, it's just typed `unknown`. Sloppy wording, cheap reword.

## One thing that changed under us

`apps/obsidian` **on main now has Vitest** — `vitest.config.mts` and the exact scripts I removed at your request two weeks ago. Merging main brings it back for free (your branch's net package.json change is empty, so no conflict). That makes a test cheap, and a test is the strongest available answer to "cooked up?" — it converts the claim into a pinned invariant.

## The decision that drives everything

Whether to keep the schema-fallback work hinges on one thing I can't settle alone: **do we actually care about canvas files this plugin didn't write?** If tldraw-in-obsidian interop is real, schema-less files are plausible and the guard earns its place. If not, it's speculative defensive code on an already scope-stretched PR, and Michael's instinct is correct.

CONTEXT: apps/obsidian (tldraw 3.14.2) currently adds a `url` prop to the text shape's props schema, with a custom `TextShapeWithLinkUtil`, a store migration backfilling `url: ""`, a forked EditLinkDialog and an `edit-link` action override. A reviewer asks us to explore storing the link in `shape.meta.url` instead, to "keep the existing props schema and avoid backfilling existing text shapes", hoping it "reduces the amount of custom code we need to maintain".

1. **Does meta avoid a migration?** Confirm how `meta` is validated — find the shape record validator (`@tldraw/tlschema`, `createShapeValidator` / `TLBaseShape`) and show that `meta` is permissive (JsonObject) so an absent `meta.url` needs no backfill and no schema change. State clearly whether existing files would load untouched.

2. **What stops working.** The stock UI is gated on props, not meta:
   - `useHasLinkShapeSelected` (`tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts` ~line 173) — show the exact predicate.
   - `EditLinkMenuItem` (`tldraw/src/lib/ui/components/menu-items.tsx`) and where it is rendered in `DefaultContextMenuContent`.
   - `EditLinkDialog` (`tldraw/src/lib/ui/components/EditLinkDialog.tsx`) — its guard and its `editor.updateShapes({props:{url}})` write.
   - the `edit-link` action (`tldraw/src/lib/ui/context/actions.tsx`).
   For each, say precisely what we would have to build ourselves if the value lived in `meta` instead of `props`.

3. **Net custom-code comparison.** Enumerate, concretely, what each approach requires:
   - **props approach (current):** custom shape util, migration, forked dialog, action override, vendored hyperlink button.
   - **meta approach:** what exactly? Can any stock UI be reused at all, or does the menu item have to be hand-built too?    Give a side-by-side count of files and roughly how many lines each approach needs, and say which is genuinely less custom code. Be honest if the reviewer's expectation is backwards.

4. **Other consequences of meta:** does `meta` survive copy/paste, duplicate, undo/redo, and the app's own save path (`createRawTldrawFile` serialises `store.allRecords()` in `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/tldraw.ts`)? Does `convertToDiscourseNode` (`apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/convertToDiscourseNode.ts`) preserve or drop meta vs props? Does anything else in apps/obsidian already use `shape.meta` — grep and report precedent.

5. **Forward/backward compatibility:** with meta, what happens when an older plugin build opens a file containing `meta.url`? Compare to the props approach, where an older build throws `Unexpected property` and renders a blank canvas.

Give a clear bottom-line recommendation with the trade-offs stated plainly.

  It is a **module-level `const Set`, never exported** (verified: `dist-esm/index.mjs` export list has `linkUrl` but not `validLinkProtocols`). So there is no runtime mutation route — you cannot `T.validLinkProtocols.add("obsidian:")`. **A patch is the only way to change tldraw's own `T.linkUrl`.** Note this is not the only route to the *feature*: the branch's current `textLinkUrl` in `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/textShapeLink.ts:32` builds an independent validator from `T.string.check(...)`, which needs no patch.
  
  Invasiveness of (a): **low** — one line per dist flavour, 2 files, no type changes (`dist-esm/index.d.mts:102` `declare const linkUrl: Validator<string>` is unaffected).
  
  Security note: patching `validLinkProtocols` to a bare `"obsidian:"` is *wider* than what the branch ships. `textShapeLink.ts:16-17` deliberately restricts to `obsidian://open?file=…` because a bare `obsidian:` check "would also admit action URIs like advanced-uri's commandid". A patch can encode the same narrowing, but `validLinkProtocols` is a protocol-only Set — you'd have to patch the `linkUrl` check body, not just the Set, to keep that restriction. That makes (a) meaningfully more than a one-word edit.
  
  ### (b) Does (a) fix `EditLinkDialog`?
  **Yes — verified, no second patch needed.** `tldraw/dist-esm/lib/ui/components/EditLinkDialog.mjs:2` does `import { T, track, useEditor } from "@tldraw/editor"`, and `@tldraw/editor/dist-esm/index.mjs:12` is `export * from "@tldraw/validate"`. There is exactly one `@tldraw/validate@3.14.2` in the store, symlinked from editor. `validateUrl` at `EditLinkDialog.mjs:15` calls `T.linkUrl.isValid`, so it picks up the patched Set. Likewise the store-side validator `TLGeoShape.ts:83` `url: T.linkUrl` and the geo migration at `TLGeoShape.ts:184` (`if (!T.linkUrl.isValid(props.url)) props.url = ''`) both become obsidian-aware — which is exactly the "consistent for text and geo" the reviewer asked for, and it also closes a real hazard: an unpatched `T.linkUrl` would let that migration silently blank obsidian URLs.
  
  ### (c) Give the text shape a `url` prop at the library level
  Files that would change:
  1. `@tldraw/tlschema/…/dist-esm/shapes/TLTextShape.mjs` — add `url: T.linkUrl` to `textShapeProps` (verified `src/shapes/TLTextShape.ts:28-35` has no `url`, unlike `TLGeoShape.ts:59,83`).
  2. Same file — add a `Versions.AddUrl` entry + migration `up` to `textShapeMigrations` (current ids: `RemoveJustify:1, AddTextAlign:2, AddRichText:3`).
  3. `@tldraw/tlschema/…/dist-cjs/shapes/TLTextShape.js` — same, twice.
  4. `@tldraw/tlschema/dist-*/index.d.*` — add `url: string` to `TLTextShapeProps`.
  5. `tldraw/…/dist-esm/lib/shapes/text/TextShapeUtil.mjs` — `component()` currently returns a bare `<RichTextLabel>` (verified `src/lib/shapes/text/TextShapeUtil.tsx:116-149`, no `url`, no `HyperlinkButton`); would need wrapping in a fragment plus `<HyperlinkButton url={…}/>`, mirroring `GeoShapeUtil.tsx:228`.

That subclass route makes the stock `edit-link` action light up for free, because the action is gated on shape props, not shape type — verified at `tldraw/src/lib/ui/context/actions.tsx:150-160` and `EditLinkDialog.tsx:35` (`'url' in selectedShape.props`).
  
  ## 4. Upgrade / maintenance risk
  
  Span per option:
  | Option | Packages | Dist files (esm+cjs) | Type files |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | (a) validation only | 1 (`@tldraw/validate`) | 2 | 0 |
  | (b) | 0 extra — falls out of (a) | 0 | 0 |
  | (5) export `HyperlinkButton` (+`EditLinkDialog`) | 1 (`tldraw`) | 2 | 1–2 |
  | (a)+(5) combined | 2 | 4 | 1–2 |
  | (c) library-level text `url` | 2 (`@tldraw/tlschema`, `tldraw`) | 4–6 | 2 |
  
  `@tldraw/editor` needs no patch in any option (it only re-exports validate).
  
  Version keying: `tldraw@2.4.6` / `@tldraw/state@2.4.6` style exact keys are what you'd use, so a bump to 3.15.x makes the patch **unused**, and with `allowUnusedPatches: false` (pnpm-workspace.yaml:5) `pnpm install` **errors out**. Fail-loud, as you expected. If instead a range key is used (`@tldraw/validate@^3.14.2`, the `@blueprintjs/core@^3.50.4` style), the patch is re-applied to the new version and fails on context mismatch — a different, also loud, failure.
  
  The empirical precedent is unambiguous: the embed-hostname patch (`79322e44`) was killed by the next tldraw upgrade (`278324c6`). One version's lifetime.
  
  **Documented policy: there is none.** I grepped `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `apps/obsidian/AGENTS.md` and `.github/` for "patch" — the only hits are `workflow_dispatch` in GH workflow files. There is no `PR_GUIDELINES.md` at the repo root. The only adjacent guidance is `apps/obsidian/AGENTS.md:3-5`:
  > "## Dependencies — Prefer existing dependencies from package.json."
  
  Nothing endorses or forbids patching. So the reviewer's "we already do this" is precedent-by-practice (5 live patches), not policy.
  
  ## 5. Is `HyperlinkButton` still unexported in 3.14.2?
  
  **Yes — verified.** `grep -n "HyperlinkButton" dist-esm/index.d.mts dist-esm/index.mjs dist-cjs/index.d.ts` in `tldraw@3.14.2` returns **zero hits**.   **`EditLinkDialog` is also unexported** (same grep, zero hits) — so the vendored `TextLinkDialog.tsx` (214 lines) has the same justification as the vendored button.
  
  **Would an export-only patch let us drop the vendored copy? Partially — and this is the crux.**
  
  - It is the **smallest possible patch** and it is *exactly* the shape of the existing `tldraw@2.4.6.patch` (add an import line + an entry in the export list in `dist-esm/index.mjs`, plus a `declare` in the `.d.ts`). ~3 files, ~8 lines, no behaviour change, no schema change. Lowest upgrade risk of every option here, and it's the change most likely to be accepted upstream, which would retire the patch entirely.
  - **But stock `HyperlinkButton` is a plain `<a href={url} target="_blank">`** (verified, `HyperlinkButton.tsx:18-30`) with no click interception. The branch's vendored copy exists for two reasons, and only one is "tldraw doesn't export it": the comment at `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx:32` says exactly that, but lines 43-46 add `event.preventDefault()` for `obsidian:` hrefs, because "falling through hands the URI to the OS handler, which runs it against the reader's vault." An export-only patch **does not** give you that. So it drops the vendored *dialog* cleanly, and drops the vendored *button* only if the click behaviour is solved another way — which is the other agent's scope, so I'm flagging the dependency rather than resolving it.
  
  **My read, stated as inference:** the highest-value / lowest-risk combination is (a) + (5) — patch `validLinkProtocols`/`linkUrl` in `@tldraw/validate@3.14.2` (2 files, gets text *and* geo consistency and fixes the stock dialog for free per §3b) and patch `tldraw@3.14.2` to export `EditLinkDialog` and `HyperlinkButton` (3 files). Keep the app-level `TextShapeWithLinkUtil` subclass; **do not** pursue (c). Total: 2 packages, 5 files, no schema change — comparable in size to the `tldraw@2.4.6` patch already in the tree. Caveats to raise with the reviewer: (i) patching `linkUrl` to accept bare `obsidian:` is *wider* than the deliberately narrow `obsidian://open?file=` allowlist the branch ships, so the patch must edit the check body, not just the Set; (ii) an export-only patch does not remove the need for custom click handling.

  ## 1. Does `meta` avoid a migration? — YES, unambiguously

  `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-2228-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-obsidian/node_modules/.pnpm/@tldraw+tlschema@3.14.2_react-dom@18.2.0_react@18.2.0__react@18.2.0/node_modules/@tldraw/tlschema/src/shapes/TLBaseShape.ts:20` — `meta: JsonObject`

  props: props ? T.object(props) : (T.jsonValue as any),
  meta:  meta  ? T.object(meta)  : (T.jsonValue as any),
  ```

  `/…/@tldraw+editor@3.14.2…/node_modules/@tldraw/editor/src/lib/config/createTLStore.ts:140-150` forwards only `props` and `migrations` to `SchemaPropsInfo`; `meta` is dropped on the floor. So for every shape type in this app, `createShapeValidator` is called with `meta === undefined` → `meta` is validated as `T.jsonValue`, i.e. "any JSON". (`SchemaPropsInfo` declares an optional `meta` field at `…/tlschema/src/createTLSchema.ts:43-47`, but nothing in the editor's util pipeline populates it.)

  `/…/@tldraw+validate@3.14.2/node_modules/@tldraw/validate/src/lib/validation.ts:299-303` and `:335-341`, `throw new ValidationError('Unexpected property', [key])`. That is exactly why the current branch needs `textLinkMigrations.ts`.

The reviewer is right on this point.
  
  ---
  
  ## 2. What stops working — all stock link UI is props-gated
  
  ### `useHasLinkShapeSelected`
  `apps/obsidian/node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173-188`:
  ```ts
  const onlySelectedShape = editor.getOnlySelectedShape()
  return !!(
    onlySelectedShape &&
    onlySelectedShape.type !== 'embed' &&
    'url' in onlySelectedShape.props &&
    !onlySelectedShape.isLocked

Note `editor.updateShapes` supports partial `meta` merges identically to props — `applyPartialToRecordWithProps`, `…/editor/src/lib/editor/Editor.ts:10685-10691` (`if (k === 'props' || k === 'meta')`).

Neither `props.url` nor `meta.url` is carried over. No differentiator; pre-existing gap either way.
  - **Precedent in apps/obsidian:** yes, `shape.meta` is already the app's chosen place for out-of-band shape data:
    - `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/shapes/DiscourseRelationShape.tsx:1147-1148` — `meta: { ...shape.meta, … }`

    (`apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/TldrawView.tsx:109` is file-level `TLData.meta`, not shape meta — different thing.)
    So `relationInstanceId` is an exact existing precedent for "app-specific value on an otherwise-stock shape, stored in meta, no migration".
  
  ---

Yes — on 2026-09-14, at plan stage, before any code.

**The decision was `props.url`, for two stated reasons:**

> **Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`.** `meta` needs no migration (it's `T.jsonValue`) but would require hand-rolling the menu item and dialog — exactly the "separate text-shape implementation" the ticket forbids.

It was inherited rather than reached independently: ENG-2227 (the Roam twin) had settled it the same day, and its checkpoint records the reasoning — the ticket says "reuse the geo-shape link code path instead of creating a separate text-shape implementation", and `props.url` is the key that unlocks tldraw's stock UI, since `useHasLinkShapeSelected` gates on `'url' in shape.props`. Paying one migration buys the menu item, its label, icon, placement and eligibility gate for free, in three menus.

**That checkpoint also wrote down the condition to revisit:**

> *Revisit if:* we ever need text links to survive an extension rollback.

That condition has now fired, and Michael found it from the other direction.

**And one of my two reasons was wrong.** I said meta forces hand-rolling "the menu item and dialog". The dialog is needed either way — `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`, so the 214-line fork exists because of page-link support, not because of props-vs-meta. The real marginal cost of meta is only the menu item plus a gate hook, ~40 lines. So the argument I leaned on was roughly half as strong as I stated.

## What the research says now

Net code is **~60-70 lines lighter** under meta, not the big simplification Michael hopes for — a custom shape util is required either way, because the util is what renders the icon. On his actual framing, "reuses more of tldraw", meta is **backwards**: it forfeits all three stock menu entries.

But the decisive trade isn't line count, it's compatibility:

| | `props.url` (current) | `meta.url` |
|---|---|---|
| Old build opens a new file | `Unexpected property: url` → **blank canvas** | loads fine, ignores the link, **round-trips it intact on save** |
| Migration + schema-fallback plumbing | ~57 lines | **gone** — which also deletes the code Michael called "suspicious" |
| URL validation | enforced at load by the schema | only on write — needs a **render-time guard**, or `javascript:` in a hand-edited file reaches `<a href>` |

Canvas files are plain markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions, so the blank-canvas mode is the serious one. There's also direct precedent: `relationInstanceId` already lives in `shape.meta` in this plugin.

Two further findings worth knowing before you decide:

- **A patch is viable and cheap for the *validator*.** Patching `validLinkProtocols` in `@tldraw/validate@3.14.2` (2 files) makes `obsidian://` work for text *and* geo consistently, and fixes the stock dialog for free — which would let us delete our dialog fork. Michael's remembered embed-hostname patch is real but was deleted by the very next tldraw upgrade, so it survived exactly one version.
- **Click behaviour is genuinely inconsistent today**, and he's right to flag it. Discourse nodes: cmd+click → new tab, shift+click → sidebar. Our text link: cmd+click → **sidebar**. Same modifier, different destination.

My recommendation is to switch to `meta.url` — it answers his question, deletes the schema work he objected to, and fixes the rollback hazard — combined with the validator patch so the dialog fork goes too.

content.text:
Yes — and it's the cheapest patch on the table. But two corrections to the premise.

**The line you linked doesn't exist in our version.** In 3.14.2, `utils/shapes/shapes.ts` contains only `getTextLabels`. On `main` that file has been refactored to hold `isShapeWithLink()` / `getSelectedLinkShape()`, with line 17 being `export type TLShapeWithLink = ExtractShapeByProps<{ url: string }>`. That refactor is newer than what we ship.

**And upstream doesn't help us anyway**: both helpers are `@internal` (unexported), and both still read `shape.props.url` only — neither looks at `meta`. So there's no extensibility hook coming for free, and an upstream PR would be a feature request rather than a small export.

## What a patch would actually touch in 3.14.2

The check is inline and duplicated across three logical sites (each ×2 for esm/cjs):

| Site | Purpose | Patchable for meta? |
|---|---|---|
| `menu-hooks.mjs:127` — `useHasLinkShapeSelected` | the eligibility gate | **yes, ~1 line** |
| `EditLinkDialog.mjs:27` | dialog's own guard — returns `null` | yes, but substantive |
| `EditLinkDialog.mjs:75` | writes `props: { url }` | yes, but substantive |

So patching **just the gate** — 2 files, one line each — makes **Edit link** appear in all three stock menus (context, main, actions) for a meta-based text shape, in tldraw's own position inside the Edit submenu. The stock *dialog* still won't work with meta, because it's separately gated and writes to props.

That's fine, though: **we need our own dialog regardless**, since `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`. Our `edit-link` action override already points the action at it.

## Why this matters for the meta decision

This removes the main cost I'd assigned to meta. Earlier I said meta forfeits all three stock menu entries and costs ~40 lines of hand-built menu item and gate hook. With a 2-line patch, it keeps them:

**`meta.url` + gate patch** → no migration, no schema-fallback plumbing (the code Michael called suspicious disappears), no blank-canvas-on-rollback, *and* stock menu placement. It answers both halves of his comment at once — store in meta, and reuse stock components via a small patch, exactly the precedent he cited.

Still needed under that combo, unavoidably: the custom shape util (it's what renders the icon), the dialog fork, the vendored button (we need click interception so `obsidian:` never reaches the OS handler), and a **render-time URL guard** — because `meta` is `T.jsonValue`, nothing validates it at load, so a hand-edited file could otherwise put `javascript:` into an `<a href>`.

Optionally, patching `validLinkProtocols` in `@tldraw/validate` (2 more files) would make `obsidian://` valid for **geo** shapes too — the text/geo consistency Michael asked for. Note it does *not* let us drop the dialog fork under meta, since the dialog is props-bound either way.

**One risk to state plainly:** the very refactor you linked is what will break this patch on upgrade — the check moves out of `menu-hooks` into `shapes.ts`. It fails loudly (`allowUnusedPatches: false`), not silently. Precedent is not encouraging: the embed-hostname patch Michael remembers survived exactly one tldraw version before being deleted.

Want me to write this up as the full rework plan — meta + gate patch + click-modifier alignment — or post it to Michael's thread first as a reply for him to sign off on?

content.text:
## The dialog fork

`TextLinkDialog.tsx` — **214 lines**. tldraw doesn't export `EditLinkDialog` (zero hits in `dist-esm/index.d.mts`), so it's a near-verbatim copy of theirs: the input, the `https://` auto-prefix, the doubled-paste correction, the Clear/Save state machine. The only real change is `validateUrlForShape`, which accepts `obsidian://` for text shapes while keeping geo on tldraw's strict `T.linkUrl`.

## The vendored button

`HyperlinkButton` inside `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` — about 55 of its 121 lines. Also a copy, because `HyperlinkButton` isn't exported either. It reproduces tldraw's `<a class="tl-hyperlink-button">` markup so text links look identical to geo links, and adds two things tldraw's version doesn't have:

- `handleClick` — intercepts `obsidian:` hrefs and calls `preventDefault()`, so the URI never reaches the OS handler
- `stopUnlessShift` — tldraw's own trick so a plain click doesn't drag the shape, but shift still reaches the select tool

Worth noting for the patch discussion: **exporting them wouldn't delete either one.** The stock dialog is hard-wired to `T.linkUrl` and to `props`; the stock button takes no `onClick`, so we can't wrap it to add interception. An export-only patch is the smallest patch but buys the least. The thing that would actually delete the 214-line dialog is patching the *validator* — and only if we stay on `props`, since the stock dialog reads and writes props.

## On the render-time guard

Your instinct is half right, and the half that's wrong is the one that matters.

Validating in the dialog is worth doing — it's what disables Save and shows "Invalid URL". But it only covers values that arrive *through our dialog*. Under `meta`, nothing validates at load, and a value can reach `meta.url` by at least four other routes:

- a hand-edited canvas file — these are plain `.md` with a JSON block, which users edit and sync between machines
- a file written by an older or newer build, or another tool
- copy/paste or duplicate of a shape (meta is preserved through both — verified in the research)
- any future code path that writes meta without going through the dialog

The sink is `<a href={url}>` inside Electron. So `javascript:` in a hand-edited file would render as a live link with no UI ever having validated it.

That's precisely the safety net `props` gives us for free — the schema rejects a bad URL at load, which is why **no render guard is needed on the current `props` implementation**. Losing it is a real cost of moving to meta, and it belongs on the ledger alongside "no migration".

The fix is one line, reusing the function we already have:

```tsx
if (!isAllowedTextLinkUrl(url)) return null;
```

So: not either/or, and not much work. Dialog check for UX, sink check for safety.

Net, if we go meta + gate patch, the honest inventory is: custom shape util (~65 lines, needed either way to render the icon), vendored button (~55), dialog fork (214), render guard (1) — and we delete the migration, the schema-fallback plumbing, and the rollback hazard.

Want me to write that up as the full plan, or post it to Michael's threads first?

content.text:
Checked both overlays — and there's an important wrinkle in the precedent.

**Both existing overlays are selection-scoped.** `RelationsOverlay` uses `getOnlySelectedShape()` (`RelationOverlay.tsx:22`), and so does `DragHandleOverlay` (`:102`). Neither iterates the page. So the pattern exists, but only for "one shape, recomputed on selection + camera change" — nobody here has done an always-on, per-shape overlay.

That said, **yes, this works, and it's the biggest simplification on the table.**

## What it buys

If the icon is an overlay, we never touch tldraw's text shape at all. Combined with `meta`, that deletes:

- `TextShapeWithLinkUtil` — 121 lines
- `baseShapeUtils` — 21 lines, *and* the "two lists that nothing asserts agree" hazard I had to write a comment about
- the migration, the schema-fallback plumbing, the swap assertion

Which leaves the dialog fork as the only sizeable custom piece. That is precisely the "reduce the amount of custom code we need to maintain" Michael asked for — far more so than meta alone.

## What it costs

The overlay sits above the canvas in viewport space, so four things that in-shape rendering gets for free become ours:

- **Rotation** — `getShapePageBounds` is axis-aligned, so on a rotated text shape the icon lands wrong. Geo's rotates with the shape. (Fixable with `getShapePageTransform`, but it's us doing it.)
- **Stacking** — the overlay draws above *every* shape, so a link icon would show through a shape stacked on top of its text.
- **Frame clipping** — a text shape clipped by a frame would still show its icon outside the frame.
- **Culling** — tldraw culls off-screen shapes automatically; an always-on overlay would recompute all linked shapes on every camera change. At realistic canvas sizes (a handful of links) this is a non-issue; I'd only flag it, not weight it.

## One design question it forces

Always-on or hover/selection-scoped?

- **Always-on** matches geo and keeps the icon as the *only* signal that a text shape is linked.
- **Hover-scoped** matches how Discourse nodes already work — their "Open in sidebar" button appears on hover (`DiscourseNodeShape.tsx:398`) — and sidesteps rotation/stacking/clipping almost entirely, since you'd only position one shape at a time.

These pull against each other, and it's exactly the tension in Michael's review: "mirror Discourse node behaviour" and "stay closer to the stock link UI" point in opposite directions here. The asymmetry that decides it for me: a Discourse node is *visibly* a node even without its hover button, whereas a linked text shape looks like plain text. Hover-only would make links undiscoverable.

**My recommendation: always-on overlay + `meta.url` + the 2-line gate patch.** That's no schema change, no migration, no custom shape util, stock menu item in its stock position, and the dialog fork as the one remaining copy. I'd accept the rotation/stacking/clipping edge cases and note them in the PR.

Want me to write that up as the plan, or put it on Michael's thread first?

# ENG-2228 — Rework text-shape links: meta storage + overlay affordance

## Context

PR [#1442](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1442) is green on CI but sits at `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Michael asked us to stop and compare approaches before committing to a schema change, and left three inline objections — all of them on the schema-fallback plumbing (`canvasFileSync.ts:70`, `tldraw.ts:57`, `tldraw.ts:90`), not on the link feature.

His two substantive asks, and what the investigation found:

**"Explore storing the link in `meta.url`."** Correct on the part that matters. `meta` is validated as `T.jsonValue` (a shape util can never supply a meta validator — `createTLStore.ts:140-150` forwards only `props` and `migrations`), so existing files load untouched: no schema change, no migration, no fallback plumbing. He is *backwards* on the reuse argument — `props.url` is the key that unlocks tldraw's stock link UI, and meta forfeits it — but that is recoverable with a two-line patch (below). The decisive argument is one neither of us made initially: with `props`, a file written by the new build and opened by an **older** build throws `Unexpected property: url` and renders a **blank canvas**; with `meta` it loads fine and round-trips the link intact. Canvas files are plain markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions, so that failure mode is the real risk. ENG-2227's checkpoint had already recorded the trigger — *"revisit if we ever need text links to survive an extension rollback"*.

**"Render the icon from an overlay instead of a custom shape."** This is the larger win and it came from Trang, not the original review. With the icon in `InFrontOfTheCanvas`, we never touch tldraw's text shape at all — the custom shape util, the shape-util swap and its sync hazard all disappear.

Together these cut the diff from ~523 lines to roughly ~300 and remove every line Michael flagged.

## Design

Store the link at `shape.meta.url` on the **stock** text shape. Render the affordance as a canvas overlay. Keep the forked dialog (needed regardless — `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`). Patch one line of tldraw so the stock **Edit link** menu item still appears.

### 1. Delete the props approach

Remove entirely: `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts`, `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts`. Revert `utils/tldraw.ts` (`schemaBeforeAppMigrations`, `APP_MIGRATIONS`, the `??` fallback) and `utils/canvasFileSync.ts` back to their pre-PR state, restoring `...defaultShapeUtils` at both registration sites. This answers all three of Michael's inline comments directly — the code he called suspicious ceases to exist.

Drop the `.dg-text-hyperlink-button` rule from `styles.css`; the overlay positions itself. Keep `EXTERNAL_LINK_ICON_SVG` in `src/icons.ts`.

### 2. New `overlays/TextLinkOverlay.tsx`

Follows `overlays/RelationOverlay.tsx` — a full-size `pointer-events: none` container, children positioned with `editor.pageToViewport()` inside a `useValue` so they track the camera. One difference from both existing overlays: those are selection-scoped (`getOnlySelectedShape`), this one iterates `editor.getCurrentPageShapes()` filtered to `type === "text" && meta.url`, because the icon is the only signal a text shape is linked.

Register it in `TldrawViewComponent.tsx` alongside the existing two:

```tsx
InFrontOfTheCanvas: () => (
  <>
    <RelationsOverlay … />
    <DragHandleOverlay … />
    <TextLinkOverlay plugin={plugin} />
  </>
),
```

Reuse the vendored markup already in `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (the `tl-hyperlink-button` anchor + `EXTERNAL_LINK_ICON_SVG` mask) so it stays visually identical to geo links, and keep the `< 0.32` zoom hide.

**Guard the href at the sink:** `if (!isAllowedTextLinkUrl(url)) return null;`. Under `props` the schema rejected bad URLs at load; `meta` is unvalidated, so a hand-edited or synced file could otherwise put `javascript:` into an `<a href>`. One line, reusing the existing helper in `utils/textShapeLink.ts`.

Known fidelity gaps versus in-shape rendering, accepted and to be noted in the PR: the icon does not rotate with a rotated shape, is not clipped by an enclosing frame, and draws above shapes stacked over the text. Use `getShapePageBounds`; at realistic link counts the per-camera-change recompute is not a concern.

### 3. Click behaviour — align with Discourse nodes

Michael's sharpest UX point. Today a node and a text link disagree on the same modifier. Target, matching `TldrawViewComponent.tsx:389-437`:

| Gesture | Action | Helper |
|---|---|---|
| plain click | open in right sidebar | `openFileInSidebar` |
| cmd/ctrl+click | open in **new tab** | `openFileInNewTab` |
| cmd/ctrl+alt+click | open in split | `openFileInNewLeaf` |
| shift+click | sidebar, and let the pointer through so the shape shift-selects (stock tldraw) | `openFileInSidebar` |

Read modifiers off the React `MouseEvent`, call `editor.selectNone()` after opening (node parity, `:436`), and keep `preventDefault()` for **every** `obsidian:` href — not just ones that parse — so an action URI can never reach the OS handler. `http(s)`/`mailto` keep stock anchor behaviour.

### 4. Dialog — read and write `meta`

`TextLinkDialog.tsx` stays (tldraw exports neither `EditLinkDialog` nor `HyperlinkButton`). Two changes: read the initial value from `meta.url` for text shapes, and branch the write — text → `meta: { url }`, everything else → `props: { url }`. `editor.updateShapes` merges `meta` exactly as it does `props` (`Editor.ts:10685-10691`). The existing `validateUrlForShape` split already keeps geo on strict `T.linkUrl`; it now also selects the storage location.

### 5. The tldraw patch — isolated and droppable

He is *backwards* on the reuse argument — `props.url` is the key that unlocks tldraw's stock link UI, and meta forfeits it — but that is recoverable with a two-line patch (below). The decisive argument is one neither of us made initially: with `props`, a file written by the new build and opened by an **older** build throws `Unexpected property: url` and renders a **blank canvas**; with `meta` it loads fine and round-trips the link intact. Canvas files are plain markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions, so that failure mode is the real risk. ENG-2227's checkpoint had already recorded the trigger — *"revisit if we ever need text links to survive an extension rollback"*.

**"Render the icon from an overlay instead of a custom shape."** This is the larger win and it came from Trang, not the original review. With the icon in `InFrontOfTheCanvas`, we never touch tldraw's text shape at all — the custom shape util, the shape-util swap and its sync hazard all disappear.

Together these cut the diff from ~523 lines to roughly ~300 and remove every line Michael flagged.

## Design

Store the link at `shape.meta.url` on the **stock** text shape. Render the affordance as a canvas overlay. Keep the forked dialog (needed regardless — `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`). Patch one line of tldraw so the stock **Edit link** menu item still appears.

Remove entirely: `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts`, `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts`. Revert `utils/tldraw.ts` (`schemaBeforeAppMigrations`, `APP_MIGRATIONS`, the `??` fallback) and `utils/canvasFileSync.ts` back to their pre-PR state, restoring `...defaultShapeUtils` at both registration sites. Drop the `.dg-text-hyperlink-button` rule from `styles.css`; the overlay positions itself. Keep `EXTERNAL_LINK_ICON_SVG` in `src/icons.ts`.

### 2. New `overlays/TextLinkOverlay.tsx`

Follows `overlays/RelationOverlay.tsx` — a full-size `pointer-events: none` container, children positioned with `editor.pageToViewport()` inside a `useValue` so they track the camera. One difference from both existing overlays: those are selection-scoped (`getOnlySelectedShape`), this one iterates `editor.getCurrentPageShapes()` filtered to `type === "text" && meta.url`, because the icon is the only signal a text shape is linked.

  <>
    <RelationsOverlay … />
    <DragHandleOverlay … />
    <TextLinkOverlay plugin={plugin} />
  </>
),
```

# ENG-2228 — Rework text-shape links: meta storage + overlay affordance

## Context

PR [#1442](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1442) is green on CI but sits at `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Michael asked us to stop and compare approaches before committing to a schema change, and left three inline objections — all of them on the schema-fallback plumbing (`canvasFileSync.ts:70`, `tldraw.ts:57`, `tldraw.ts:90`), not on the link feature.

His two substantive asks, and what the investigation found:

**"Explore storing the link in `meta.url`."** Correct on the part that matters. `meta` is validated as `T.jsonValue` (a shape util can never supply a meta validator — `createTLStore.ts:140-150` forwards only `props` and `migrations`), so existing files load untouched: no schema change, no migration, no fallback plumbing. He is *backwards* on the reuse argument — `props.url` is the key that unlocks tldraw's stock link UI, and meta forfeits it — but that is recoverable with a two-line patch (below). The decisive argument is one neither of us made initially: with `props`, a file written by the new build and opened by an **older** build throws `Unexpected property: url` and renders a **blank canvas**; with `meta` it loads fine and round-trips the link intact. Canvas files are plain markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions, so that failure mode is the real risk. ENG-2227's checkpoint had already recorded the trigger — *"revisit if we ever need text links to survive an extension rollback"*.

**"Render the icon from an overlay instead of a custom shape."** This is the larger win and it came from Trang, not the original review. With the icon in `InFrontOfTheCanvas`, we never touch tldraw's text shape at all — the custom shape util, the shape-util swap and its sync hazard all disappear.

Together these cut the diff from ~523 lines to roughly ~300 and remove every line Michael flagged.

## Design

Store the link at `shape.meta.url` on the **stock** text shape. Render the affordance as a canvas overlay. Keep the forked dialog (needed regardless — `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`). Patch one line of tldraw so the stock **Edit link** menu item still appears.

### 1. Delete the props approach

Remove entirely: `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts`, `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts`. Revert `utils/tldraw.ts` (`schemaBeforeAppMigrations`, `APP_MIGRATIONS`, the `??` fallback) and `utils/canvasFileSync.ts` back to their pre-PR state, restoring `...defaultShapeUtils` at both registration sites. Register it in `TldrawViewComponent.tsx` alongside the existing two:

```tsx
InFrontOfTheCanvas: () => (
  <>
    <RelationsOverlay … />
    <DragHandleOverlay … />
    <TextLinkOverlay plugin={plugin} />
  </>
),
```

Reuse the vendored markup already in `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (the `tl-hyperlink-button` anchor + `EXTERNAL_LINK_ICON_SVG` mask) so it stays visually identical to geo links, and keep the `< 0.32` zoom hide.

Under `props` the schema rejected bad URLs at load; `meta` is unvalidated, so a hand-edited or synced file could otherwise put `javascript:` into an `<a href>`. | Gesture | Action | Helper |

## Verification

Static: `pnpm --filter @discourse-graphs/obsidian check-types`, `lint`, `build`, then root `pnpm ci:validate` re-run with `--force` so a warm turbo cache can't mask a failure. Check for new lint *warnings* on added lines — CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings while local lint exits 0.

In Obsidian, via `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` (drive real input events — programmatic `store.put` fires no store listeners, so it never triggers the autosave):

1. **Edit link** appears in the Edit submenu for a text shape; absent with two shapes selected or when locked.
2. Dialog accepts an `obsidian://open?…file=…` URL and enables Save; rejects `javascript:`, `obsidian://advanced-uri?commandid=…` and other non-`open` action URIs.

# ENG-2228 — Rework text-shape links: meta storage + overlay affordance

## Context

PR [#1442](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1442) is green on CI but sits at `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Michael asked us to stop and compare approaches before committing to a schema change, and left three inline objections — all of them on the schema-fallback plumbing (`canvasFileSync.ts:70`, `tldraw.ts:57`, `tldraw.ts:90`), not on the link feature.

His two substantive asks, and what the investigation found:

**"Explore storing the link in `meta.url`."** Correct on the part that matters. `meta` is validated as `T.jsonValue` (a shape util can never supply a meta validator — `createTLStore.ts:140-150` forwards only `props` and `migrations`), so existing files load untouched: no schema change, no migration, no fallback plumbing. He is *backwards* on the reuse argument — `props.url` is the key that unlocks tldraw's stock link UI, and meta forfeits it — but that is recoverable with a two-line patch (below). The decisive argument is one neither of us made initially: with `props`, a file written by the new build and opened by an **older** build throws `Unexpected property: url` and renders a **blank canvas**; with `meta` it loads fine and round-trips the link intact. Canvas files are plain markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions, so that failure mode is the real risk. ENG-2227's checkpoint had already recorded the trigger — *"revisit if we ever need text links to survive an extension rollback"*.

**"Render the icon from an overlay instead of a custom shape."** This is the larger win and it came from Trang, not the original review. With the icon in `InFrontOfTheCanvas`, we never touch tldraw's text shape at all — the custom shape util, the shape-util swap and its sync hazard all disappear.

Together these cut the diff from ~523 lines to roughly ~300 and remove every line Michael flagged.

## Design

Store the link at `shape.meta.url` on the **stock** text shape. Render the affordance as a canvas overlay. Keep the forked dialog (needed regardless — `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`). Patch one line of tldraw so the stock **Edit link** menu item still appears.

### 1. Delete the props approach

Remove entirely: `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts`, `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts`. Revert `utils/tldraw.ts` (`schemaBeforeAppMigrations`, `APP_MIGRATIONS`, the `??` fallback) and `utils/canvasFileSync.ts` back to their pre-PR state, restoring `...defaultShapeUtils` at both registration sites. This answers all three of Michael's inline comments directly — the code he called suspicious ceases to exist.

Drop the `.dg-text-hyperlink-button` rule from `styles.css`; the overlay positions itself. Keep `EXTERNAL_LINK_ICON_SVG` in `src/icons.ts`.

### 2. New `overlays/TextLinkOverlay.tsx`

Follows `overlays/RelationOverlay.tsx` — a full-size `pointer-events: none` container, children positioned with `editor.pageToViewport()` inside a `useValue` so they track the camera. One difference from both existing overlays: those are selection-scoped (`getOnlySelectedShape`), this one iterates `editor.getCurrentPageShapes()` filtered to `type === "text" && meta.url`, because the icon is the only signal a text shape is linked.

Register it in `TldrawViewComponent.tsx` alongside the existing two:

```tsx
InFrontOfTheCanvas: () => (
  <>
    <RelationsOverlay … />
    <DragHandleOverlay … />
    <TextLinkOverlay plugin={plugin} />
  </>
),
```

Reuse the vendored markup already in `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (the `tl-hyperlink-button` anchor + `EXTERNAL_LINK_ICON_SVG` mask) so it stays visually identical to geo links, and keep the `< 0.32` zoom hide.

**Guard the href at the sink:** `if (!isAllowedTextLinkUrl(url)) return null;`. Under `props` the schema rejected bad URLs at load; `meta` is unvalidated, so a hand-edited or synced file could otherwise put `javascript:` into an `<a href>`. One line, reusing the existing helper in `utils/textShapeLink.ts`.

Known fidelity gaps versus in-shape rendering, accepted and to be noted in the PR: the icon does not rotate with a rotated shape, is not clipped by an enclosing frame, and draws above shapes stacked over the text. Use `getShapePageBounds`; at realistic link counts the per-camera-change recompute is not a concern.

### 3. Click behaviour — align with Discourse nodes

Michael's sharpest UX point. Today a node and a text link disagree on the same modifier. Target, matching `TldrawViewComponent.tsx:389-437`:

| Gesture | Action | Helper |
|---|---|---|
| plain click | open in right sidebar | `openFileInSidebar` |
| cmd/ctrl+click | open in **new tab** | `openFileInNewTab` |
| cmd/ctrl+alt+click | open in split | `openFileInNewLeaf` |
| shift+click | sidebar, and let the pointer through so the shape shift-selects (stock tldraw) | `openFileInSidebar` |

Read modifiers off the React `MouseEvent`, call `editor.selectNone()` after opening (node parity, `:436`), and keep `preventDefault()` for **every** `obsidian:` href — not just ones that parse — so an action URI can never reach the OS handler. `http(s)`/`mailto` keep stock anchor behaviour.

### 4. Dialog — read and write `meta`

`TextLinkDialog.tsx` stays (tldraw exports neither `EditLinkDialog` nor `HyperlinkButton`). Two changes: read the initial value from `meta.url` for text shapes, and branch the write — text → `meta: { url }`, everything else → `props: { url }`. `editor.updateShapes` merges `meta` exactly as it does `props` (`Editor.ts:10685-10691`). The existing `validateUrlForShape` split already keeps geo on strict `T.linkUrl`; it now also selects the storage location.

### 5. The tldraw patch — isolated and droppable

`useHasLinkShapeSelected` gates on `'url' in shape.props`, so a meta-based link would show no **Edit link** item. One line in each of two dist files restores it:

- `dist-esm/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.mjs:127`
- `dist-cjs/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.js:158`

Added as `patches/tldraw@3.14.2.patch` via `pnpm patch`, keyed `tldraw@3.14.2` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — the repo already has five such patches, including `tldraw@2.4.6.patch`, and version-keying means apps/roam's 2.4.6 is untouched.

This buys the stock menu item in its stock position in all three menus. **Treat it as a separate, reversible decision**: if Michael would rather not patch, drop it and hand-build the item in `CustomContextMenu.tsx` with a local gate hook (~40 lines) — nothing else in this plan changes. Two honest caveats for the PR: upstream has already refactored this check into `utils/shapes/shapes.ts` (still `props`-only, still `@internal`), so the patch **will** break on the next tldraw upgrade — loudly, since `allowUnusedPatches: false`; and the embed-hostname patch Michael remembers survived exactly one tldraw version.

### 6. Housekeeping

Merge `origin/main` first — the branch is 52 commits behind, and only `styles.css` is touched on both sides. Then reply on all three of Michael's threads explaining what was removed and why.

## Open items (not mine to close)

- **Loom.** Michael asked for a detailed video covering adding a text shape from the toolbar, adding the link, and converting a linked text shape to a discourse node. I can produce CDP screenshots for the PR body via the `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` and `pr-evidence` skills, but the Loom itself is yours to record.
- **Tests stay out** per your earlier call. Flagging once, without re-litigating: the render-time guard is now the *only* thing standing between a hand-edited `meta.url` and an `<a href>`, and `apps/obsidian` on main has since gained Vitest. Your call.
- **Convert To still drops the link** — `convertToDiscourseNode.ts` builds a fresh shape and copies neither `props.url` nor `meta.url`. Pre-existing under both designs; Michael's Loom request covers this path, so expect it to come up.

## Verification

Static: `pnpm --filter @discourse-graphs/obsidian check-types`, `lint`, `build`, then root `pnpm ci:validate` re-run with `--force` so a warm turbo cache can't mask a failure. Check for new lint *warnings* on added lines — CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings while local lint exits 0.

In Obsidian, via `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` (drive real input events — programmatic `store.put` fires no store listeners, so it never triggers the autosave):

1. **Edit link** appears in the Edit submenu for a text shape; absent with two shapes selected or when locked.
2. Dialog accepts an `obsidian://open?…file=…` URL and enables Save; rejects `javascript:`, `obsidian://advanced-uri?commandid=…` and other non-`open` action URIs.
3. Icon renders beside the text, tracks pan and zoom, and hides below 0.32 zoom.
4. Each modifier opens in the right place per the table, matching a Discourse node in the same canvas.
5. Link survives close/reopen, and the saved markdown contains `meta.url` and **no** `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link` sequence.
6. **Rollback check — the reason for this rework:** open a canvas containing `meta.url` with a build that predates it; it must render normally and preserve the link on save.
7. Geo regression: a geo shape still takes a web URL and still rejects `obsidian://`.

Before trusting any run, grep the built bundle for a symbol you just added — another worktree's dev watcher shares the same vault plugin directory.

**Revert to pre-PR** — `utils/canvasFileSync.ts`; `utils/tldraw.ts` (keep only the `externalContentHandlers` export it needs).

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config
- packages/typescript-config: Shared tsconfig.jsons
- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Agent-created Engineering tickets

For all agent-created Engineering tickets, including direct Linear tool calls and tickets created through other skills, use [dg-create-engineering-ticket](.agents/skills/dg-create-engineering-ticket/SKILL.md). Create them in `Ticket Draft` with exactly one workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group: `Created by Claude`, `Created by Codex`, or `Created by LLM` for another or unknown agent. Record the creation skills actually used in `Notes`, and verify those fields after creation. If no skill was used, record `Created with: direct agent workflow (no skill)` and still apply the same review rules.

The requesting human reviews intent, scope, acceptance criteria, and ticket-writing standards before approving a move to `Triage` or `Backlog`. Keep the provenance label after approval. See the skill for transitions and missing-configuration handling. This applies to new tickets; do not retrospectively classify existing tickets.

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues. For PRs over 400 changed lines, excluding tests, include a concise split justification, main review entry points, and testing path in Reviewer brief.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Required standards

- Read and follow [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md) and the nested `AGENTS.md` files that apply to changed files before editing or reviewing code.
- Follow [PR_GUIDELINES.md](PR_GUIDELINES.md) for scope, verification, and review requirements. General code standards live in the style guide; app-specific instructions remain in nested `AGENTS.md` files.
- Before handoff or requesting review, run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` from `.agents/skills/dg-pr-adherence-check/SKILL.md` against the final diff and available PR metadata. Resolve findings or report them explicitly, including missing evidence. Rerun affected checks after changes.
